card: Converts walletprocesspsbt to accept an options dictionary as its second parameter while maintaining full backward compatibility for existing positional and named invocations. Currently, walletprocesspsbt requires up to four trailing positional parameters, three of which are booleans, making calls error-prone and requiring any future options to append yet another positional parameter. The pull request also updates the RPC framework to allow different types per parameter alias, validates types based on the specific alias used, and emits oneOf schemas in OpenRPC. This cleanly unblocks future configuration additions to walletprocesspsbt, such as PR 32857.
changed_since_previous: Includes handling in transformNamedArguments for mixed positional and named calls, enforces strict type checking against the exact parameter name passed, checks options before wallet sync and PSBT decoding, and adds full unit and functional test coverage.
evidence: PR description explains the usability and extensibility problem: 'walletprocesspsbt takes four settings after the PSBT, three of them booleans, so a positional call reads walletprocesspsbt "psbt" true "ALL" true false, and each new setting becomes one more positional parameter (#32857 would add a sixth).'
PR description highlights that unblocking cleaner parameter additions enables PR #32857 and planned follow-ups for descriptorprocesspsbt and createwallet.
problem: walletprocesspsbt takes four positional parameters after the PSBT string (three of which are booleans), making invocations clumsy and requiring any new configuration parameter to append yet another positional argument. The RPC framework also lacked support for assigning different types to parameter aliases and enforcing type checks per alias, preventing RPC methods from replacing positional parameters with an options object without breaking backward compatibility.

risk.why: A bug in RPC parameter resolution or argument transformation could break existing automated scripts and callers using walletprocesspsbt with positional or named arguments.

scope_notes: Touches core RPC infrastructure in src/rpc/ (request parsing, argument transformation, type checking, and OpenRPC generation) to enable the wallet RPC signature migration.
summary: Converts walletprocesspsbt to accept an options dictionary as its second argument, grouping sign, sighashtype, bip32derivs, and finalize while maintaining backward compatibility for existing positional and named calls. Extends the RPC framework to support distinct types per parameter alias, validates parameter types against the specific alias supplied by name, and emits oneOf schemas in OpenRPC documentation. Also updates transformNamedArguments to correctly handle mixed positional and named arguments without triggering duplicate parameter errors.
